papers.title_in_file: An Improved Quantum Software Challenges Classification Approach using Transfer Learning and Explainable AI
papers.what_it_is: A study that classifies quantum developer questions from Q&A forums into challenge categories with fine-tuned transformer models and SHAP.

assertions.value: The authors state that transfer-learning models such as BERT and DistilBERT are effective without data augmentation, while CNN and MLP models rely heavily on augmentation.
quotes: TL models like BERT and DistilBERT are effective out-of-the-box due to their extensive pre-training on large corpora, making them robust even with limited or imbalanced datasets.
traditional DL models such as CNN and MLP rely heavily on data augmentation techniques
assertions.certainty_reason: One study on one dataset of quantum developer posts.
assertions.reader_inference: The abstract also reports 95% accuracy for BERT and DistilBERT; that sentence sits in two-column text that could not be copied cleanly, so the figure is not in the value.

assertions.value: The authors report that the CNN classifier reached an overall accuracy of 86% with augmented data, compared to only 51% without augmentation.
quotes: The CNN model showed a significant improvement when trained with augmented data, achieving an overall accuracy of 86%, compared to only 51% without augmentation.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that 2829 developer discussions on quantum software engineering were collected from Q&A platforms and annotated, and that Cohen's kappa was 0.46.
assertions.anchor: Section 3 method and Section 7 threats to validity
quotes: 2829 developers' discussions on QSE collected from Q&A platforms were added in a Microsoft Excel document to be annotated by the first and third authors
achieving a Cohen's kappa of 0.46 indicating substantial agreement
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own dataset size and annotation agreement (Section 3 and threats to validity).
assertions.reader_inference: Elsewhere the paper calls kappa 0.46 moderate agreement; here it says substantial.

assertions.value: The authors state that researcher bias is significant in this study because the authors and ChatGPT labeled and analyzed the discussions.
quotes: the potential for researcher bias is significant, as the first, second, and third authors, along with an AI model such as ChatGPT, labeled and analyzed developer discussions
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this limit in their threats to validity.

papers.title_in_file: A hardware efficient quantum residual neural network without post-selection
papers.what_it_is: Proposes an ancilla-controlled quantum residual network (QResNet) trained in simulation on image classification, with an adversarial robustness test.

assertions.value: The authors report accuracies of 99% and 80% for binary and multi-class classification on MNIST, CIFAR and SARFish, and state that the model requires 10x fewer gates.
quotes: achieving accuracies of 99% and 80% for binary and multi-class classifications, respectively.
however our model requires 10x fewer gates making it better suited for resource constraint near-term quantum processors.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulated results from one study; the gate comparison is the authors' own.

assertions.value: The authors report MNIST test accuracy exceeding 99% with 200 quantum gates, CIFAR-2 test accuracy of 76%, and SARFish test accuracy of 72.14%.
quotes: For MNIST, the model test accuracy is exceeding 99% within the first few epochs while requiring only 200 quantum gates.
with 76% test accuracy using substantially fewer gates.
the test accuracy is 72.14%.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulated binary classification results from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report that a 30-layer QVC-only baseline reached approximately 65% accuracy and that adding five ancilla-controlled residual blocks raised test accuracy to approximately 80%.
quotes: A QVC-only baseline consisting of 30 variational layers achieves approximately 65% classification accuracy
increasing the test accuracy to approximately 80%
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulated result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that simulation of deeper QResNet configurations was limited by classical memory constraints that scale exponentially in state-vector simulation.
quotes: simulation of deeper QResNet configurations was limited by classical high-performance computing memory constraints arising from ancilla-controlled residual operations, which scale exponentially in state-vector simulation.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this limit of their own experiments.

papers.title_in_file: Performance Benchmarking of Quantum Algorithms for Hard Combinatorial Optimization Problems: A Comparative Study of non-FTQC Approaches
papers.what_it_is: Benchmarks VQE, QAOA, QITE, ITQA, simulated annealing and D-Wave annealing on max-cut, number partitioning, knapsack and a quantum spin glass.

assertions.value: The authors report that, with default configurations, no single non-FTQC algorithm performs optimally across all problem types.
quotes: Employing default configurations, our findings reveal that no single non-FTQC algorithm performs optimally across all problem types
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical benchmark from one study with default configurations.

assertions.value: The authors report that QAOA fidelity significantly degrades for number partitioning and knapsack problems.
quotes: The QAOA fidelity significantly degrades for number partitioning and knapsack problems
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on small instances from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that QITE typically outperforms ITQA, and that success probability is highly instance-dependent.
quotes: Nevertheless, QITE typically outperforms ITQA (Fig. 2(a)).
Success probability is highly instance-dependent (Fig. 3)
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the benchmark uses default configurations and deliberately avoids algorithm-specific improvement techniques, and that more comprehensive benchmarking standards are still needed.
quotes: By employing default configurations and deliberately avoiding algorithm-specific improving techniques, this study offers a controlled reference for performance evaluation.
Further research is required to develop more comprehensive benchmarking standards
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope and limits in Section IV.

papers.what_it_is: A theory paper that proposes a way to extract dequantizability conditions from input matrices and applies it to the sparse-access input model.

assertions.value: The authors state that the paper forms a dequantizability-verifying scheme that can be applied whenever an input is given.
quotes: this paper forms a dequantizability-verifying scheme that can be applied whenever an input is given.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' summary claim in the abstract; the proofs were not re-derived here.

assertions.value: The authors state that storage of a matrix in a quantum-accessible data structure does not by itself imply efficient quantum access to that matrix.
quotes: storage alone does not imply the existence of certain efficient quantum access to that matrix
assertions.certainty_reason: Lemma 1 (Lemma 7), Section 1.1.

assertions.value: The authors state that their corollary requires that there exists dequantization for some non-trivial sparse-access input model, and that the triad would not grand-unify QML algorithms.
quotes: it necessitates that there exists dequantization for some non-trivial sparse-access input model
would not "grand-unify" QML algorithms at all
assertions.certainty_reason: Corollary 15 following Theorem 14.
assertions.reader_inference: The corollary holds under the paper's assumption that the instance is un-dequantizable.

assertions.value: The authors state that proving or disproving that no classical algorithm dequantizes the sparse Hermitian case would either limit or clarify the implications of their corollary.
quotes: will either limit or clarify the implications of Corollary 15
assertions.certainty_reason: The open problem is stated in Section 5.

papers.title_in_file: A resource theory of asynchronous quantum information processing
papers.what_it_is: A theory paper on port-based teleportation that defines a hierarchy of communication models and computes optimal fidelities for several state families.

assertions.value: The paper shows that a bipartite state can break the one-way classical teleportation threshold if and only if it can be done using the trivial decoding map of discarding subsystems.
quotes: Thus, a bipartite state can break the one-way classical teleportation threshold if and only if it can be done using the trivial decoding map of discarding subsystems.
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated as a main result in the abstract and proved in the paper.

assertions.value: The authors state that values for isotropic states demonstrate strict inclusions in the hierarchy of the PBT models.
quotes: These values enabled us to demonstrate strict inclusions in the hierarchy
assertions.certainty_reason: Derived for isotropic states in Section IV A.

assertions.value: The authors state that their analysis focuses on isotropic states, bipartite graph states and symmetrized EPR states, for which they compute tight bounds on the optimal teleportation fidelities.
quotes: Our analysis focuses specifically on the PBT power of isotropic states, bipartite graph states, and symmetrized EPR states, and we compute tight bounds on the optimal teleportation fidelities for such states.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own scope in the abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that identifying the minimal type of pre-processing beyond PBTq needed for non-classical teleportation of two-qubit states is an open problem.
quotes: it is an interesting open problem to identify the minimal type of pre-processing beyond
assertions.certainty_reason: Open problem stated in the Conclusion.

papers.title_in_file: Variational Quantum Algorithm for Constrained Topology Optimization
papers.what_it_is: Proposes a single-loop variational quantum algorithm for topology optimization with two entangled registers and demonstrates it on small truss and beam problems.

assertions.value: The authors propose a variational quantum algorithm for constrained topology optimization with a single-loop parallel search for the optimal configuration that also satisfies the physical constraints.
quotes: a novel variational quantum algorithm for constrained topology optimization is proposed, which allows for the single-loop parallel search for the optimal configuration that also satisfies the physical constraints.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own proposal, stated in the abstract.

assertions.value: The authors report that the algorithm was demonstrated on three truss structures and two MBB beams, using at most 12 qubits and 22 Hermitian operators in the problem Hamiltonian.
quotes: The proposed VQA is demonstrated with compliance minimization problems involving three truss structures and two MBB beams.
the VQA is implemented with at most 12 qubits and 22 Hermitian operators in the problem Hamiltonian.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the scope of their demonstrations in Section 5.

assertions.value: The authors state that the gate-count factor depends on the sparsity of stiffness matrices, the degrees of element connectivity, and the number of qubits.
quotes: This factor depends on the sparsity of stiffness matrices, the degrees of element connectivity, and the number of qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Gate complexity analysis in Section 2.3.

assertions.value: The authors report that the optimization is sensitive to the Lagrange multipliers and Bayesian optimization settings, and that larger structures require more qubits and deeper circuits.
quotes: The results show that the optimization is sensitive to the hyperparameters including the Lagrange multipliers and the Bayesian optimization settings.
Solving TO problems with larger structures requires more qubits and deeper circuits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Limits stated by the authors in Section 5.

papers.title_in_file: AI Agents for Variational Quantum Circuit Design
papers.what_it_is: Tests LLM agents (Claude 3.7 Sonnet and Llama 3.3 70B) that propose and evaluate variational circuit designs in simulation.

assertions.value: The authors state that the results show the agents were able to improve performance over iterations for all three QNN architectures, with varying degrees of success.
quotes: The results show that the agents were able to achieve this for all three architectures, although with varying degrees of success.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from a few simulated runs.

assertions.value: The authors report that Llama 3.3 70b reached a best test RMSE of 0.021 with 48 parameters in the VQC on the Simple QNN, outperforming Claude 3.7 Sonnet's best of 0.0326.
quotes: LLama 3.3 70b was able to achieve a best test RMSE of 0.021 with 48 parameters in the VQC, outperforming Claude 3.7 Sonnet's best of 0.0326.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single reported runs, one per model.

assertions.value: The authors report that on the Lie-EQGNN benchmark more trainable VQC parameters did not reliably give higher test AUC, with the best candidates between 250 and 400 parameters.
quotes: increasing the number of trainable VQC parameters does not reliably increase test AUC.
between 250 and 400 parameters
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one agent run.

assertions.value: The authors state that the evaluation is restricted to simulated QNNs and a simplified regression task.
quotes: our evaluation is restricted to simulated QNNs and a simplified regression task
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the Limitations paragraph of Section 5.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Approximate and Quantum Walk Optimization Approaches to Set Balancing
papers.what_it_is: Maps set balancing to an Ising/QUBO model and compares six QAOA mixers in simulation, plus an entropy-based post-processing step.

assertions.value: The authors report that, averaging approximation ratios over 20 iterations per mixer at depth p = 5, the most consistent performers were the Grover mixer and the SWAP mixers.
quotes: took the average of the approximation ratios for 20 iterations per mixer, each with depth p = 5.
the most consistent performers are Grover Mixer and SWAP Mixers.
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result from one study on small instances.

assertions.value: The authors state that the scaled-exponential Pauli-string decomposition outperforms standard QAOA mixers at higher depths.
quotes: it outperforms standard QAOA mixers at higher depths
assertions.certainty_reason: Reported simulation result; the numeric range is cut off in the text.

assertions.value: The authors state that the program is run in a quantum simulator.
quotes: We are running the program in a quantum simulator
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated by the authors in the QAOA experiment section.

assertions.value: The authors state that future work may focus on extending these techniques to larger instances.
quotes: Future work may focus on extending these techniques to larger instances
assertions.certainty_reason: Stated in the Conclusion.
